_note: 80D for the parents: insurance and preventive check-ups (not a notified health scheme — s.126(2)(b) names none; corrected by W-075d2, D-145) up to ₹25000 in aggregate (s.126(2)(b), p.161); medical expenditure up to ₹50000 (s.126(2)(d)); together "The amount of sum referred to in sub-section (2) shall not exceed ₹ 50000 in aggregate of the sum specified under sub-section (2)(a) and (c) or aggregate of the sum specified under sub-section (2)(b) and (d)" (s.126(4), p.162). Medical expenditure on a senior citizen only "if no amount has been paid to effect or to keep in force the health insurance of such person" (s.126(7)); a senior citizen is "an individual resident in India who is of the age of sixty years or more at any time during the relevant tax year" (s.2(100), p.20). ChapterEightNode uses this row where no person covered is a senior citizen. Old regime only (s.202(2)(a)(xii), p.227). TY 2026-27 and TY 2025-26; the 1961 counterpart, s.80D, is the TY 2025-26 version (W-075d2). D-136. TY 2025-26: Income-tax Act, 1961 s.80D(2) (thc p.341): "(b) the whole of the amount paid to effect or to keep in force an insurance on the health of the parents or parents [sic, the consolidation's text] of the assessee or any payment made on account of preventive health check-up of the parent or parents of the assessee as does not exceed in the aggregate twenty-five thousand rupees" — like s.126(2)(b), no scheme; "(d) … medical expenditure incurred on the health of any parent of the assessee … fifty thousand rupees", only for an uninsured senior citizen; (b) with (d) within fifty thousand rupees. sources/2026-10-07-chapter-via.md B11–B13. D-145. In every regime as a row; the new regime forbids it through DIS-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION, whose basis REG-NEW-TAX-REGIME-NO-EXEMPTION (S2 s.202(2)(a); 1961 s.115BAC(2)(i)) every explanation cites (D-166).
